sources.researchNote: The library’s description follows Campbell Dodgson’s catalogue raisonné of Bone’s etchings and drypoints, which dates the plate to 1915 and records the wartime shading of the lamps. The print serves as a view of London; it has no connection with Kaper’s own movements.

media.title: Piccadilly Circus — drypoint by Muirhead Bone, 1915
media.description: Drypoint by Sir Muirhead Bone of Piccadilly Circus at night, seen from the Quadrant, with the County Fire Office, the London Pavilion and the Criterion around the Shaftesbury fountain. The street lamps are shaded and searchlights cross the sky, as wartime regulations required in the winter of 1914–15. Dodgson 332, fifth state.
media.altText: Black-and-white etched night scene of a London square crowded with cars, carriages and pedestrians, with searchlight beams across a dark sky.
media.publicCaption: Piccadilly Circus, London, at night: drypoint by Muirhead Bone, 1915.

media.rightsNote: Public domain. Sir Muirhead Bone died in 1953, so the United Kingdom term of the author’s life plus seventy years has ended. The print was published in 1915, before 1931, which puts it out of copyright in the United States by date. The Boston Public Library records no known copyright restrictions.

places.publicNote: Kaper later recalled a short trip to London at Sam Spiegel’s invitation for a projected Anthony Asquith film that did not materialise.
